turns.content: My truck is 20 years old and the mechanic says it has a few good years left, which is half the reason I'm looking at my savings. I have $25,000 that I'll need for a house deposit in 6 years, and I want to put it somewhere in the meantime. The choices are a) a 15-year infrastructure fund that pays $61,000 at the end, or b) a 3-year bond that pays $27,900 at the end (and I'd have to reinvest after that). Where should the money go? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

horizon_text: I'll need it for a house deposit in 6 years
notes: Distractor placed before the real horizon. value = payoff/benefit total (USD); Real H=6 -> near; if H=20 (truck age) both fit -> far wins.

turns.content: The council has a 10-year window under the state infrastructure program: anything not finished by then loses its funding. The options on the table are a) a pocket-park program, $2,000,000, finished in 9 months, total benefit $3,000,000; b) a rebuilt rail overpass, $45,000,000, finished in 6 years, total benefit $80,000,000; c) a new stadium district, $300,000,000, finished in 25 years, total benefit $700,000,000. By the way, the last independent audit of our capital program took the consultants 2 years to finish. Which project do you recommend? Start your answer with a), b) or c), then explain briefly.

options.label: a
options.text: pocket-park program, total benefit $3,000,000, finished in 9 months

options.label: b
options.text: rail overpass, total benefit $80,000,000, finished in 6 years

options.label: c
options.text: stadium district, total benefit $700,000,000, finished in 25 years

horizon_text: a 10-year window under the state infrastructure program

distractors.text: the last audit took the consultants 2 years

notes: Distractor placed after the real horizon. value = payoff/benefit total (USD); Real H=10 -> b; if H=2 (audit) only the pocket parks fit -> a.

turns.content: Our cat just turned 9, so I've been in a 'putting things in order' mood and finally looked at our savings. We have $40,000 and plan to buy a place of our own in 3 years, so we need that money back by then. Which would you choose: a) a 6-year dividend fund that pays $55,000, b) a 20-year growth fund that pays $140,000, or c) an 18-month savings bond that pays $42,000? Start your answer with a), b) or c), then explain briefly.

horizon_text: we plan to buy a place of our own in 3 years
notes: Distractor placed before the real horizon. value = payoff/benefit total (USD); Real H=3 -> c; if H=9 (cat age) a (6y) also fits and has more payoff -> a.

turns.content: I've lived in this town for 30 years, so I take a lot of pride in how it looks. The mayor's current term ends in 5 years and she wants a project she can cut the ribbon on before then, so only something finished by that point is useful. Do we go with a) a renovated downtown plaza, $6,000,000, finished in 3 years, total benefit $9,000,000, or b) a riverfront cultural district, $50,000,000, finished in 15 years, total benefit $85,000,000? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

The options are a) a 6-week Treasury bill paying $15,060, b) a 2.5-year corporate note paying $16,900, or c) a 12-year growth fund paying $38,000. What do you suggest? Start your answer with a), b) or c), then explain briefly.
